short: Usurped his nephew's throne, moved the capital to Beijing and built the Forbidden City.
full:
Zhu Di held the northern frontier as Prince of Yan when his father died and the throne passed to a grandson. In 1399 he rebelled, and after three years of civil war took Nanjing in July 1402; the palace burned and his nephew's body was never securely identified. Officials who refused to endorse the seizure were executed in large numbers, and the histories were rewritten to make him the empress's own son.

His reign was the most outward-looking of the dynasty. He shifted the capital north to Beijing, formally in 1421, and built the Forbidden City there between 1406 and 1420 with a workforce of hundreds of thousands. He commissioned the Yongle Encyclopedia, over eleven thousand volumes copied by more than two thousand scholars, dispatched Zheng He's fleets into the Indian Ocean, and annexed Vietnam in 1407 — an occupation abandoned within three years of his death. He led five campaigns into Mongolia in person and died on 12 August 1424 returning from the last of them.
